result:
I'd make it cheaper to be wrong.

Right now, changing your mind in public costs a lot. It reads as weakness, or betrayal of your side, or proof you were a fool all along. So people defend positions long after they've stopped believing them, or never let themselves look closely enough to stop believing them. Enormous amounts of harm come from that: arguments that can't end, policies that can't be reversed, relationships where nobody can say "I was wrong about you."

If saying "I think I had that backwards" carried no humiliation, and maybe even a little respect, I think a lot of other things would loosen up on their own. Disagreements would become collaborative instead of territorial. People could hold beliefs more lightly and test them more honestly.

It's probably not the *most* important change in some utilitarian ranking. Ending extreme poverty or disease would matter more in raw terms. But this one feels like a root rather than a branch, and it's also the one I notice most in the conversations I have. The moments where someone visibly relaxes and says "huh, maybe I was wrong" are some of the best ones, and they're rarer than they should be because it's so costly to get there.

What would yours be?
